---
title: Work with FITS files from a terminal
description: Use imred to copy sections, combine images, and apply image arithmetic.
---

Use `imred copy`, `imred comb`, and `imred arith` for FITS file operations.
These examples expand the command outlines in the original Sphinx docs.

**Inputs:** install `astroimred[full]` and replace the example paths with your
own FITS files. These commands create output files; they do not overwrite
existing outputs unless you add `--overwrite`.

## 1. Inspect the available options

```bash
imred --help
imred copy --help
imred comb --help
imred arith --help
```

The installed command's help reflects that installed version. The online
API follows `main`, which may be newer than the released package.

## 2. Copy an image section

```bash
imred copy science.fits science-cutout.fits --trimsec '[1:16,1:16]'
```

FITS sections use one-based, inclusive `(x, y)` bounds. This example selects
the first 16 pixels on both axes. Quote the section so the shell passes it
unchanged. See [`imcopy`](../api/imutil.imcopy.imcopy.qmd) for extensions,
output dtype, and header behavior.

## 3. Combine calibrated exposures

```bash
imred comb 'calibrated-*.fits' combined.fits --combine average --reject none
```

Quote the glob so `imred` receives one input expression. Use frames on a
common pixel grid with compatible units. This command requests an average
without outlier rejection; it does not calibrate or align the inputs for you.

Choose clipping and normalization using the
[`imcombine` reference](../api/imutil.imcombine.imcombine.qmd), or follow the
[Python combination example](combine-images.qmd) first. Diagnostic spread
images describe the retained samples; they are not propagated uncertainty.

## 4. Apply image arithmetic

```bash
imred arith science.fits - master-bias.fits science-bias-subtracted.fits
```

See [`imarith`](../api/imutil.imarith.imarith.qmd) for alignment and error
handling. Use the [calibration tutorial](calibrate-images.qmd) when you need
the bias, dark, and flat stages together. The CLI has no `ccdred` subcommand;
the combined calibration pipeline is a Python API.
